questions.question: What is this warning about?
questions.answer: It is about why this book can be hard to understand.

questions.question: If a person cannot understand all of the book, what can he still get?
questions.answer: He can still get some benefit from it.

questions.question: What picture is used to help us understand this idea?
questions.answer: A person in a garden picking only some fruit.

questions.question: Why can the person in the garden not take all the fruit?
questions.answer: His hands cannot reach all of it.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for the book being hard to understand?
questions.answer: Five reasons.

questions.question: In the first reason, who did the writer mainly write for?
questions.answer: For himself.

questions.question: In the first reason, did he write to match everyone else’s way of thinking?
questions.answer: No. He wrote from his own understanding.

questions.question: In the second reason, what makes the topics hard?
questions.answer: They are very wide, very deep, and sometimes very long.

questions.question: Why might some people not understand everything at one time?
questions.answer: Because the ideas are too big and deep to grasp all at once.

questions.question: In the third reason, why can one sentence become very long?
questions.answer: To keep a big truth together without breaking it apart.

questions.question: What may be needed before one proof is given?
questions.answer: A lot of steps to get ready for it.

questions.question: In the fourth reason, what makes the discussion longer?
questions.answer: Many proofs and signs are included.

questions.question: About how many proofs might be used sometimes?
questions.answer: Ten or twenty.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, when did these ideas come to the writer?
questions.answer: During Ramadan.

questions.question: What problems did the writer have while writing?
questions.answer: He was upset, sick, and wrote quickly.

questions.question: Why did he not fix and rearrange the writing later?
questions.answer: He felt he should not change it by his own thoughts.

questions.question: What is one more thing that made the book harder to understand?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic.

questions.question: What happened to the first part that was fully in Arabic?
questions.answer: It was taken out and made into a separate work.

questions.question: What is the main message of the warning at the beginning?
questions.answer: Not everyone will understand everything, but everyone can gain something.

questions.question: What does the garden example teach us?
questions.answer: A person may not get all of something good, but can still receive a helpful share.

questions.question: Does the passage say the book is made for only one kind of reader?
questions.answer: No. It is for different readers with different levels.

questions.question: How many causes of difficulty are named?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What is the first cause in simple words?
questions.answer: The writer recorded what he understood for himself.

questions.question: How is this book different from books written to fit other people’s ideas?
questions.answer: It follows the writer’s own understanding instead.

questions.question: What special subject in the second cause makes the book extra hard?
questions.answer: It talks about Allah’s oneness in a very full and great way.

questions.question: Which is harder for many people: small simple ideas or broad deep ideas?
questions.answer: Broad deep ideas.

questions.question: What does the third cause show about very long sentences?
questions.answer: They may be used to hold one big truth together.

questions.question: Why might a proof need many beginning parts first?
questions.answer: Because the truth being shown is large and needs setup.

questions.question: What is the fourth cause mostly about?
questions.answer: There are many proofs and pieces of evidence.

questions.question: How can too many proofs affect some readers?
questions.answer: It can make the discussion too long and hard for them.

questions.question: What does the fifth cause tell us about the writer’s condition?
questions.answer: He was troubled and sick when he wrote.

questions.question: Did he write slowly with careful editing, or quickly without revising much?
questions.answer: Quickly without revising much.

questions.question: How did the writer feel about changing the words later?
questions.answer: He felt it was not right to change them by his own will.

questions.question: What language in some sections may have made reading harder for some people?
questions.answer: Arabic.

questions.question: What was done with the fully Arabic first station?
questions.answer: It was separated into its own work.

questions.question: If a child understands only part of this book, is that still worthwhile?
questions.answer: Yes. Even part of it can still help.

questions.question: What kind of note is this passage: a story, a warning, or a set of rules?
questions.answer: A warning.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with a warning?
questions.answer: To prepare readers for a difficult book.

questions.question: What hopeful idea is given before the five causes?
questions.answer: Nobody will leave without getting some share.

questions.question: What does the fruit stand for in the garden example?
questions.answer: The good understanding a reader can gain.

questions.question: What do longer arms in the example mean?
questions.answer: Some people can understand more than others.

questions.question: What is the first reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own personal understanding.

questions.question: What can happen when a book is not written to match other people’s minds?
questions.answer: Some readers may find it harder to follow.

questions.question: What is the second reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: The topics are very big, deep, and long.

questions.question: Why are big topics harder to understand all together?
questions.answer: Because they cannot be taken in all at once by everyone.

questions.question: What is the third reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: One sentence may become very long to protect one whole truth.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the truths in the book?
questions.answer: They are large and connected.

questions.question: What is the fourth reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: It gives many proofs and evidences.

questions.question: What might a reader with a small attention span feel when there are many proofs?
questions.answer: The reader may feel it is too long or confusing.

questions.question: What is the fifth reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: The writer was in a hard condition and wrote fast without revision.

questions.question: Name one part of that hard condition.
questions.answer: He was ill.

questions.question: Name another part of that hard condition.
questions.answer: He was distressed.

questions.question: Besides illness and haste, what else added to the difficulty?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic.

questions.question: What happened to the section written fully in Arabic?
questions.answer: It was removed and turned into a separate work.

questions.question: What should a reader expect from this passage before reading the book?
questions.answer: The reader should expect some parts to be difficult.

questions.question: Even if the whole book is not understood, what does the passage say will still happen?
questions.answer: The reader will still receive some benefit.

questions.question: In the garden picture, is the garden only for one person?
questions.answer: No. It is for others too.

questions.question: What does that teach about readers?
questions.answer: Different readers can take different amounts from the same book.

questions.question: How many causes of difficulty are listed?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What is one clue from the first cause that the book is personal in style?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own observations.

questions.question: Why might a very personal style be harder for some readers?
questions.answer: It may not match how they usually think.

questions.question: In the second cause, what three words best describe the topics?
questions.answer: Wide, deep, and long.

questions.question: In the third cause, why is one truth not broken into tiny pieces?
questions.answer: So the full meaning stays together.

questions.question: What can make one proof take a long time to explain?
questions.answer: It needs many beginning parts first.

questions.question: In the fourth cause, what happens when many evidences are added?
questions.answer: The explanation becomes longer.

questions.question: Why can that be hard for some minds?
questions.answer: They may not be able to keep up with so much at once.

questions.question: In the fifth cause, what holy month is mentioned?
questions.answer: Ramadan.

questions.question: What was the writer’s health like while writing?
questions.answer: He had several illnesses.

questions.question: Did the writer feel fully in control of the writing by his own choice?
questions.answer: No. He felt he was not simply writing by his own will.

questions.question: How did that feeling affect revision?
questions.answer: He did not want to rearrange or correct it by his own ideas.

questions.question: What two language-related details are mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic, and one fully Arabic section was made separate.

questions.question: What is one big idea of the whole warning?
questions.answer: A hard book can still help every reader.

questions.question: What example from nature is used to explain that idea?
questions.answer: A garden with fruit.

questions.question: If someone can reach only a few fruits, does that mean the garden is useless to him?
questions.answer: No. The few fruits are still enough to help him.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for the difficulty?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: In the first reason, what did the writer put down in the book?
questions.answer: His own observations and understanding.

questions.question: What was not his main goal in writing?
questions.answer: Matching the ideas of other people.

questions.question: In the second reason, what subject is presented in a very full way?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why can such a subject be hard for some readers?
questions.answer: It is very broad and deep.

questions.question: In the third reason, why might a single sentence last for a page or more?
questions.answer: To keep one large truth whole.

questions.question: What does “many preliminaries” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Many early explanations are needed first.

questions.question: In the fourth reason, what makes the book feel long?
questions.answer: It often gives a lot of proofs.

questions.question: Why might ten or twenty proofs be too much for some readers?
questions.answer: It can be hard for them to understand so many.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, what was happening in the writer’s life while he wrote?
questions.answer: He was upset and sick.

questions.question: How did he write because of that condition?
questions.answer: He wrote in a hurry.

questions.question: What did he not do to the first draft?
questions.answer: He did not revise it.

questions.question: What feeling stopped him from changing the writing much?
questions.answer: He felt it should not be fixed by his own personal choice.

questions.question: What final detail shows why some readers might struggle with the book’s language?
questions.answer: Parts of it were in Arabic.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this beginning passage?
questions.answer: To explain why understanding the book may be hard.

questions.question: Does the passage give only a warning, or also some encouragement?
questions.answer: It gives both warning and encouragement.

questions.question: What is the encouragement?
questions.answer: Everyone can still receive some share from it.

questions.question: How does the garden example help a young reader understand this?
questions.answer: It shows that getting some fruit is still good, even if not all of it.

questions.question: What number of causes should the reader remember?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What is the first cause about?
questions.answer: The book comes from the writer’s own understanding and experience.

questions.question: What is the second cause about?
questions.answer: The ideas are very great and deep.

questions.question: What is the third cause about?
questions.answer: Long sentences and long setup for one proof.

questions.question: What is the fourth cause about?
questions.answer: The use of many proofs and evidences.

questions.question: What is the fifth cause about?
questions.answer: The writer’s hard condition while writing.

questions.question: Which cause mentions the widest and deepest topics?
questions.answer: The second cause.

questions.question: Which cause mentions very long sentences?
questions.answer: The third cause.

questions.question: Which cause mentions ten or twenty proofs?
questions.answer: The fourth cause.

questions.question: Which cause mentions sickness and haste?
questions.answer: The fifth cause.

questions.question: Which cause shows that the writer was not trying to write for everybody’s level?
questions.answer: The first cause.

questions.question: What month is connected to the coming of the treatise’s lights?
questions.answer: Ramadan.

questions.question: What writing choice made the book harder besides the writer’s sickness?
questions.answer: He did not go back and revise and correct it.

questions.question: What happened to the part written completely in Arabic?
questions.answer: It became a separate work.
